In a shocking finish to a surreal Democratic primary for Wisconsin governor, Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley narrowly defeated front-running Rep. Francesca Hong in the state's primary election Tuesday, Aug. 11.

With about 99% of the vote in, Crowley holds a lead of more than 3,000 votes over Hong, according to DecisionDeskHQ.

Crowley has 313,348 votes, or 39.8%, while Hong has 310,037, or 39.4%

It's a remarkable comeback for Crowley, who had dropped out of the race July 8, polling in the single digits, before resurrecting his campaign July 17 with Gov. Tony Evers' support.

Hong, a democratic socialist, had a substantial lead in polls throughout the weeks before the primary, though many Democratic voters said they were undecided. Evers and others in the party pushed for Crowley, contending he's more electable against Tiffany than Hong is.

Crowley will face Republican U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany in the Nov. 3 general election.

While that was the big primary race, there were lots of other races throughout the state – and the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel and USA TODAY NETWORK-Wisconsin were here for them.

# United Steelworkers use 'bat light' to promote Biden

Malcolm Hall

The Repository

Updated Oct. 9, 2020, 8:21 a.m. ET

**CANTON** Posted for about a half hour high on the exterior of a downtown 13-story office building was a written promotion for the presidential campaign of Joseph Biden and Kamala Harris.

"Biden-Harris" was projected in light onto the building wall by an image projector placed on a sidewalk in the 100 block of Tuscarawas Street E.

The United Steelworkers brought their "bat light" promotion project to the Canton area Thursday as the labor union urged anyone passing by on the downtown streets to exercise their right to vote Nov. 3. And at the same time they were promoting the Democratic presidential ticket.

"Right now, that is the important message we want to get," said Amber Miller, a part of the United Steelworkers Political Action Committee. "However, you choose to vote, make sure you are ready."

The United Steelworkers team made a handful of stops in the Canton area to project their promotional message. Other selected stops included the Pro Football Hall of Fame and the McKinley Monument.

"We looked where our (union) members were," said Miller, who is from the United Steelworkers' Pittsburgh office. "We wouldn't go out in rural areas and do this. We are not going in areas where we know this message would not be very welcome. We are not here to antagonize."

Biden, a former vice president, and Harris, a member of the U.S. Senate representing California, comprise the Democratic Party ticket seeking to oust Republican President Donald Trump and Vice President Mike Pence.

Trump, during the 2016 election, won Stark County with 55.8% of the vote. His Democratic Party opponent, Hillary Clinton, captured 38.6% of the vote. Trump also won Ohio with 51.6% of the vote.

The United Steelworkers have been holding these image projection promotions in cities in various states of the Midwest.

"This week was kind of an Ohio week," Miller said.

Three concerns the union is focusing on are affordable health care, retirement security and workers' rights on the job.

Members of the union said Biden provided satisfactory responses when these concerns were expressed to him. However, Trump reportedly failed to respond to the union.

"About a month ago, we started the project," said Jess Kamm Broomell, public relations officer for the United Steelworkers. "We call it the bat light project. They are mostly get out the vote messages to remind people to get out and vote."

Upon leaving the office building, the group's next stop was another downtown site, Arrowhead Vintage & Handmade Goods in the 500 block of Cleveland Avenue NW. The image promoting the Biden-Harris campaign was projected on the wall of the single-story building with a colorful mural in the background.

"This is great, this is awesome," said David Sherrill, owner of Arrowhead Vintage & Handmade Goods. "My social media will see 5,000 to 6,000 people."

While the promotional image was displayed on the downtown office building, it was visible from U.S. Route 30 on the south side of Canton, said Joe Plott, a unit chair of the United Steelworkers union representing rank-and-file employees at The Timken Co. bearing plant.

"I think it is encouraging because the Trump people have been so vocal," Plott said.

Miller of the United Steelworkers clarified that these promotional messages were not supplied by the Biden campaign.

"We don't coordinate with them," Miller said.

# United Steelworkers Union Shines ‘Batlight' Style Biden-Harris Logo on Trump Tower

## The light projection is part of the union's "batlight" tour which has made appearances in several battleground states

#### Published October 17, 2020 • Updated on October 18, 2020 at 10:22 pm

Courtesy United Steelworkers Union

A projector shines the words “Biden-Harris” onto Trump Tower in Chicago on Oct. 16, 2020. The United Steelworkers Union is behind the multi-state traveling campaign.

A "Biden-Harris" campaign logo was projected in light onto the Trump Tower in downtown Chicago Friday as part of the United Steelworkers' multi-state "batlight" tour to turn out the vote on Nov. 3.

The labor union used an outdoor projector to shine their endorsement of the Democratic ticket, emblazoning blue letters with the names of former Vice President Joe Biden and California Senator Kamala Harris on the 98-story high-rise above Trump's name. The "batlight" campaign, named after the famed Bat-Signal used to summon Gotham's caped crusader in times of distress, also made appearances on Wrigley Field, the Art Institute of Chicago and the Chicago Theatre.

A spokeswoman for the labor union, which represents about 850,000 members across the country, said the campaign is aimed at "encouraging workers to make a plan to vote in the upcoming general election." Launched last month, it has made appearances in several battleground states, including Michigan, Minnesota, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin.

"USW members across the country are familiar with the consequences of the broken promises they have endured for the last four years," USW International President Tom Conway said in a news release. "The president claims to have saved jobs, but his failed policies are responsible for hastening the loss of manufacturing employment."

The union says despite Trump's claims that he revived the steel industry, his policies "have been heavy on talk and massive corporate tax cuts, but light on strategic, long-term action when it comes to truly protecting American jobs." Since 2017, 37 steel mills have closed and over 10,000 jobs have been lost.

A USW Twitter account dedicated to the "batlight" tour tweeted several photos Saturday of Trump Tower adorned with the image, including the caption: "We didn’t?! We did!! And it felt so good. (The most action that sad, half-empty building’s seen in a while.) Good morning Chicago."

> An eyesore no more. 🦇🔦 #USWBatLight #VOTE #BidenHarris2020 pic.twitter.com/hrydheBzJ2

The "batlight" also visited several other locations across the city including the Chicago Theatre, the Art Institute of Chicago and Wrigley Field.
